To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

pAKMN2 is the first promoter probe vector, based on highly fluorescent GFPm2+, which allows stable integration of the cloned promoter in the M. tuberculosis genome, and expression of the reporter gene in the absence of any antibiotic.

a highly fluorescent GFPm2‐based genome integration proficient promoter probe vector has been constructed, and its use for the study of minimal promoters of M.tuberculosis cell division genes has been demonstrated.
we have designed a genome integration‐proficiency promoter probe vector, pAKMN2 carrying a substrate‐free, easily scorable, highly sensitive and highly fluorescent GFPm2+.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a genome integration‐proficiency promoter probe vector, carrying a substrate independent, easily scorable, highly sensitive reporter gene, for the study of promoter activity of slow growing Mycobacterium tuberculosus during long‐term in‐vitro growth or inside macrophage.
the development of novel molecular tools for genetic manipulation of M. smematis and M. tubercolosis.
the development of a highly sensitive, substrate‐independent reporter gene, for use in promoter probe vectors for the study of slow‐growing mycobacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pAKMN2 vector is a genome integration proficient, promoter probe vector, that can be used to study promoters of any myobacterial species in long‐term in vivo or in vitro growth conditions.
the pAKMN2 vector is useful for studying the expression of cloned promoters in M. tubercolosis and related species.
pAKMN2 can be used as a highly sensitive genome integration‐proficiency promoter probe vector for the study of M. tuberculosis promoters in infected host macrophages.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the promoter probe vector, pAKMN2 is a highly fluorescent GFPm2+-based genome integration‐promoter probe vector to study M. tuberuclosis promoters inside macrophages.
the pAKMN2 is the best promoter probe vector to be used for the promoter activity studies in M. tubercolosis and other mycobacterial species.
the pAKMN2‐MtftsZ‐pAKMN2 integrants showed stable expression of GFPm 2 + from MtftsZ in vitro and inside infected macrophages, and could be detected easily by flow cytometry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed a genome‐integration‐proficient promoter‐probe vector, pAKMN2.
the pAKMN2‐derived promoter integration vector is useful for studying promoter activity in M. tobacilli in vitro and inside host cells.
pAKMN2 is an ideal promoter probe vector for studying promoters in slow growing mycobacteria, including M. t. tuberculosi s, in vitro and inside the macrophages.
